newsitem.title: UK: Shell, Enron finalise transport stake in YPFB.
newsitem.headline: Shell, Enron finalise transport stake in YPFB.

text.p: Shell International Gas Ltd announced on Monday the financial close of the capitalisation of the transportation segment of Bolivian state oil and gas company Yacimientos Petroliferos Fiscales Bolivianos (YPFB).
Shell and Enron of the U.S. were named the winning bidders in the capitalisation of the transport sector in December.
The Bolivian government privatised three operational units of YPFB, two upstream units and the transport unit, under the capitalisation system.
Winning bidders got 50 percent of the stock, and management control of each company. Instead of paying cash for the shares, they have to invest the sum they bid to help capitalise the new firm.

With financial close, the two companies jointly acquire this 50 percent stake, including 1,655 miles of existing natural gas pipelines, 1,438 miles of existing oil and liquids pipelines, and ownership in the Bolivia-to-Brazil Pipeline Project, with an equity investment of $263.5 million.
The remaining interest in the newly formed company, TRANSREDES SA, is held by the Bolivian pension funds (34 percent) and by current and former employees of YPFB (16 percent).

TRANSREDES will invest the $263.5 million over the next eight years to upgrade the existing system to meet national energy requirements, and to ensure sufficient gas can be transported to meet market demand in Brazil and to build the Bolivia-to-Brazil Pipeline Project.
Shell and Enron hold a 29 percent interest in the Bolivian portion of the project and Shell, Enron and the Bolivian pension funds together own 33 percent of the overall project.
